articles.title: Deno 2.9 Released
articles.description: A huge release for the runtime: deno desktop turns scripts and framework-based projects into native, self-contained desktop apps, quick migration from npm/pnpm/Yarn/Bun lockfiles, big test runner improvements, ~2x faster cold starts, and a target of Node.js 26 compatibility.
articles.author: Bartek Iwańczuk

articles.title: Iterating Faster on VS Code with TypeScript 7
articles.description: How the VS Code team incrementally adopted the Go-based TypeScript 7 compiler (currently in RC) while it was still being built. Type-checking the source went from 36s to 5s, with npm run watch going from 80s to ~20s.
articles.author: The VS Code Team (Microsoft)

articles.title: Why Drizzle Couldn't Publish New Releases on npm for a Month
articles.description: As well as explaining why the creators of the popular ORM ran into the problem, Evert shares some tips to see if you're at risk of the same problem, and how to avoid it entirely.
articles.author: Evert Pot

articles.title: The Shifting Line Between CSS States and JavaScript Events
articles.description: A tour of the (more than you’d think) CSS pseudo-classes that can stand in for JS event listeners, plus a look at the experimental/future event-trigger syntax.
articles.author: Daniel Schwarz

articles.title: Blocking Install Scripts is Not a Silver Bullet
articles.description: npm v12 won't run install scripts by default, but Ulises argues that only solves part of the supply chain security problem.
articles.author: Ulises Gascon

articles.title: Moving Linear from styled‑components to StyleX
articles.description: A migration away from a runtime CSS-in-JS approach yielded ~30% faster renders when navigating between pages.
articles.author: Kenneth Skovhus (Linear)

articles.title: Nub: An All-in-One Toolkit That Augments Node.js
articles.description: While Bun or Deno can replace Node, this project from Zod’s creator extends Node with nice-to-haves, like fuller TypeScript support, faster & more secure package installation, better .env handling, and a web-standard Worker.
articles.author: Colin McDonnell et al.

articles.title: Gea: A Compiler-First Reactive UI Framework
articles.description: A UI framework that goes all in on "compile the framework away": no VDOM, JSX transformed into string templates, proxy-based stores, and 'surgical' DOM patching. The big win is tiny build sizes.
articles.author: Armagan Amcalar

articles.title: <qr-code> 2.0: Web Component for Generating QR Codes
articles.description: An easy way to display QR codes in the browser using pure JavaScript. A 13 year old solution that’s been modernized and is now ESM only. Live demo.
articles.author: Eduard Castellano

articles.title: spartan/ui 1.0: shadcn/ui-Style UI Primitives for Angular
articles.description: If you’re an Angular developer who’s ever envied the copy and paste simplicity of shadcn/ui, this is for you.
articles.author: Robin Goetz

articles.description: The second preview release of npm 12 is available for testing. This is worth doing, as Colin McDonnell has already noticed npm 12 hard-errors on unrecognized keys in .npmrc files.
🔒 npm now locks 'high impact accounts' (maintainers of the most popular packages) into a 72-hour read-only mode when they change their email or use a 2FA recovery code.
The Svelte team has just posted the latest monthly Svelte update. In related news, Svelte creator Rich Harris was recently asked ▶️ for his takes on working with AI and Svelte.
🤖 AI SDK v7 – Vercel's SDK that provides an abstraction for building against any AI model provider.
Node.js v26.4 (Current) adds experimental package map support to resolve packages from a static JSON file instead of walking node_modules.
Formisch v1 RC – Schema-first, headless type-safe form state library.
Prettier 3.9, Rspack 2.1, Electron 43, ESLint 10.6, pnpm 11.9

articles.title: 🥣 The Goldilocks Customizable Select Height
articles.description: Jake walks through getting the sizing of customizable <select> elements just right. He lands on a calc-size() solution that respects intrinsic sizing while capping dimensions. A practical deep-dive with demos, CSS code examples, and fallbacks.
articles.author: Jake Archibald

articles.title: Introducing the <usermedia> HTML element
articles.description: Shipping in Chrome 151, this replaces the getUserMedia() prompt for controlling camera and microphone access. It also introduces a way to let users change their mind on blocked permissions, without the need to dig into browser settings.
articles.author: Viana and Le (Google)

articles.title: The Shifting Line Between CSS States and JavaScript Events
articles.description: A tour of the (more than you’d think) CSS pseudo-classes that can stand in for JS event listeners, plus a look at the experimental/future event-trigger syntax.
articles.author: Daniel Schwarz

articles.title: ▶  Modern UI Patterns
articles.description: A talk from the recent CSS Day conference in which Una dives into some of the newest updates in CSS and the web UI space, and also shares a UX framework of 5 principles to frame your design decisions through a modern UI lens.
articles.author: Una Kravets

articles.title: An Animated Radial Gradient Mask Over Text in CSS
articles.description: Cassidy shows us how she replicated a neat radial rings effect, using the CSS mask property along with a repeating radial gradient. Demo here. Browser support isn’t universal, but the journey she takes is interesting.
articles.author: Cassidy Williams

articles.title: Dark Mode with Web Standards
articles.description: A good technical overview on how to implement a robust dark mode for your site — one that respects OS-level preferences, but also provides a manual override.
articles.author: Ollie Williams

articles.title: ▶  Supercharge Web UX with View Transitions
articles.description: In this 50-minute talk Bramus starts off with a clear introductory overview of how View Transitions work, before “turning it up to 11” and really getting into the detail of what we can achieve with this API.
articles.author: Bramus Van Damme

articles.title: WebGL Without a GPU
articles.description: How do you render WebGL on a fleet of Linux boxes with no graphics card? A look at the CPU-emulation chain that’s available, and a Chrome flag that sped up taking a screenshot by 4x.
articles.author: Kiko Beats

articles.title: Modes and Themes That Stick: Building a Persistent Toggle Solution
articles.description: A three-layer, progressively enhanced approach to mode and theme switching.
articles.author: Stuart Robson

articles.title: Slim Select 4.0: An Advanced Select Dropdown Control
articles.description: A feature-rich select dropdown component with no dependencies. The recently released v4.0 adds a modal mode for mobile-friendly picking.
articles.author: Brian Voelker

articles.title: FixCSS: A Library to Rectify Mistakes in the Design of CSS
articles.description: TIL that the CSS Working Group has a list of ‘mistakes’ made in the design of CSS. This library sets out to rectify these failures, as explained here.
articles.author: Declan Chidlow

articles.title: <qr-code> 2.0: Web Component for Generating QR Codes
articles.description: A recently modernized, decade-old solution to display QR codes on the Web in PNG, SVG, and HTML formats (so you can style them entirely to your liking). Demo.
articles.author: Eduard Castellano

articles.title: Snipgrapher: CLI Tool to Generate Images of Code Snippets
articles.description: Whether from code files, stdin, or an inline source. It uses the powerful Shiki syntax highlighter, but with a built-in fallback option.
articles.author: Matteo Collina

articles.title: Where to Find the Colors Your Screen Can’t Show You
articles.description: We may now have fancy displays and a slew of expanding color capabilities at our disposal (P3, OKLCH, color()), but there are still real-world colors screens can’t reliably reproduce. Ryan takes us on a fascinating journey of just what those colors are: “There are around 500 species of birds with colors outside the sRGB gamut”.
articles.author: Ryan Moulton
